- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., 1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to reflect potential mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged upward trend; cap forecast growth to avoid lagging or overestimating momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often drifts toward historical mean; apply slight downward bias if recent prices are above mean, or upward if below.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in early days of the 30d window (e.g., first 5–7 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward early if sentiment is bullish, or downward if bearish.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is negative in the last 3–5 days; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is negative.
- Model overestimates when sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling; reduce forecast slope to reflect sentiment decay.
